projects.name: My CV Website
projects.description: A futuristic, interactive portfolio featuring a 3D space environment, AI chat assistant, and a hidden retro terminal OS.

caseStudy.problem: Standard static portfolios fail to demonstrate complex engineering skills or personality. I needed a platform that could serve as both a resume and a live demonstration of modern frontend capabilities.
caseStudy.solution: I built a 'living' application using the Next.js 16 App Router. It features a persistent 3D background (R3F), a context-aware AI agent (Groq Llama 3.3), and a fully functional CLI terminal Easter egg that mimics a retro OS.

architecture.description: Built on Next.js 16 (React 19) for server-side rendering and SEO. Content is managed via Sanity CMS for real-time updates without redeployment. The 3D scene runs in a separate React Context to persist across page navigation.

technicalChallenges.title: Persistent 3D Scene Navigation
technicalChallenges.description: Preventing the heavy Three.js canvas from reloading on route changes required lifting the Canvas into a global Context provider and using Next.js template files to handle page transitions smoothly over it.

technicalChallenges.title: AI Context Injection
technicalChallenges.description: The AI chat needs to know about my resume without hallucinating. I implemented a RAG-lite system that injects structured JSON data from the Sanity backend into the LLM's system prompt at runtime.

codeSnippets.title: AI Route Handler (RAG)
codeSnippets.description: Server-side route handler that constructs a context-aware prompt for the AI using live portfolio data.

codeSnippets.title: Retro Terminal Command Parser
codeSnippets.description: A custom hook-based CLI engine that handles command history, 'sudo' easter eggs, and localized output.

projects.name: CodeBase
projects.description: A developer productivity tool that scans repositories, visualizes structure, and generates context-optimized prompts for LLMs. Installable versions available for Linux (RPM).

caseStudy.problem: Preparing code context for Large Language Models (LLMs) is tedious. Developers manually open files, copy content, and format it with separators, often leading to missed dependencies or context window overflows.
caseStudy.solution: I built a native desktop GUI that visualizes the repository tree, respects `.gitignore` rules, and allows 1-click generation of formatted prompts. It features a multi-threaded file scanner and a secure content preview engine.

architecture.description: The application follows a modular architecture using `tkinter` with `ttkbootstrap` for the UI. Core logic is separated into `FileHandler` (scanning), `ContentManager` (processing), and `SecurityValidator` (safety). It utilizes a custom `ThreadSafeLRUCache` for performance and `queue.Queue` for thread-safe UI updates.

technicalChallenges.title: UI Responsiveness During Scans
technicalChallenges.description: Scanning thousands of files blocked the main UI thread. I implemented a threaded worker pattern where the scanner runs in a background thread and pushes status updates to a `queue.Queue`, which the main loop polls to update the progress bar without freezing.

technicalChallenges.title: Security & Path Traversal
technicalChallenges.description: To prevent accidental exposure of system files, I implemented a strict `SecurityValidator` that enforces path normalization (`os.path.normcase`) and checks `os.path.commonpath` to ensure all operations stay within the user's home directory.

codeSnippets.title: Thread-Safe UI Polling
codeSnippets.description: A non-blocking polling mechanism that processes callbacks from background threads on the main Tkinter event loop.

codeSnippets.title: Secure File Reading
codeSnippets.description: A centralized file reader that integrates LRU caching and security checks before file access.
codeSnippets.code:
def get_file_content(file_path, content_cache, lock, read_errors):
    normalized_path = normalize_for_cache(file_path)
    cached = content_cache.get(normalized_path)
    if cached: return cached

    if SECURITY_ENABLED:
        is_valid, error = validate_file_size(file_path)
        if not is_valid: return None

    with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as file:
        content = file.read()
        content_cache.put(normalized_path, content)
        return content

projects.name: OmniComment
projects.description: A decentralized commenting system allowing users to comment on any webpage via a Chrome Extension.

caseStudy.problem: Traditional comment systems are siloed to specific websites. Users cannot discuss content on static pages or sites that have disabled comments.
caseStudy.solution: A browser-agnostic overlay system that injects a discussion layer over any URL, synchronized via WebSockets for real-time interaction.

architecture.description: The system utilizes a Monorepo architecture separating the Server, WebApp, and Chrome Extension packages. Real-time updates are handled via Socket.IO adapted with Redis for horizontal scaling.

technicalChallenges.title: Chrome Extension Context Isolation
technicalChallenges.description: Managing authentication state between the background service worker, content scripts, and the injected IFrame required a robust message-passing interface to ensure secure token handling without exposing them to the host page.

technicalChallenges.title: Recursive Comment Threads
technicalChallenges.description: Storing and retrieving arbitrarily deep comment threads efficiently in MongoDB required complex aggregation pipelines using $graphLookup to avoid the N+1 query problem.

codeSnippets.title: MongoDB Recursive Aggregation
codeSnippets.description: An aggregation pipeline used to fetch top-level comments and efficiently graph-lookup all nested replies in a single database query.

codeSnippets.title: CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions)
codeSnippets.description: Automated quality gates ensuring strict linting (Biome) and build verification across the Monorepo workspaces before any production deployment.
codeSnippets.code:
name: Continuous Integration

jobs:
  quality-checks:
    name: Lint, Format & Build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run Biome Checks
        run: npx biome check .

      - name: Build All Workspaces
        run: npm run build --workspaces --if-present

projects.name: Video Course Platform
projects.description: A scalable video course platform with tiered user management (Admin, Client, Employee), Stripe payment integration, and Blockchain-based diploma verification.

caseStudy.problem: Current market solutions lacked a unified system for secure certificate verification alongside course delivery.
caseStudy.solution: Integrated the Polygon blockchain to mint secure, verifiable diplomas upon course completion, ensuring data integrity and GDPR compliance.

architecture.description: Monolithic Node.js/Express backend with MongoDB. React frontend. Blockchain integration via Web3.js.

projects.name: PomoZen
projects.description: An offline-first, high-performance Pomodoro timer built with React 19 and Web Workers. Features 'Zen Mode' soundscapes, local persistence, and zero-drift timing logic.

caseStudy.problem: Browser-based timers often suffer from 'time drift' when the tab becomes inactive due to browser battery-saving throttling. Additionally, most online timers require internet access and track user data.
caseStudy.solution: I architected an offline-first PWA that offloads the timing logic to a dedicated Web Worker. This ensures the timer runs precisely even when the tab is backgrounded. State is persisted locally via Zustand middleware, offering a privacy-first experience.

architecture.description: The application follows a 'Brain/Heart/Face' architecture. The 'Heart' (Timer Engine) runs in a Web Worker using Comlink. The 'Brain' (Zustand Store) manages state and persistence. The 'Face' (React UI) purely reflects the store state.

technicalChallenges.title: Main Thread Throttling
technicalChallenges.description: Browsers throttle `setInterval` on the main thread when tabs are inactive. To solve this, I moved the timer logic to a dedicated Web Worker and communicated via `postMessage` (wrapped in Comlink) to keep the UI in sync without drift.

technicalChallenges.title: Audio Policy Compliance
technicalChallenges.description: Browsers block autoplaying audio. I implemented an `AudioUnlocker` component that captures the first user interaction to unlock the AudioContext globally, allowing the alarm and ambient 'Zen Mode' sounds to play reliably.

codeSnippets.title: Web Worker Timer (Drift Prevention)
codeSnippets.description: The timer logic runs in a separate thread, exposed via Comlink, ensuring precision regardless of UI load or tab visibility.

codeSnippets.title: Zustand Persistence & Logic
codeSnippets.description: State management handles both the business logic and local storage synchronization automatically.
